items.title: 61521_David Albert Francis oral history interview
items.q: The interviewer mentions Harold Holder as a band boy for Cab Calloway; the interviewee (David Albert Francis) does not mention a personal interaction or relationship with Holder, only agreeing with the interviewer's description of Rudolph Rillis.

ctx.x: Yes, he hustled hard. He really did, too.

When he'd go in to the restaurant to buy sandwiches for us, he'd have (Inaudible) get him one. I remember when I first came with Cab Calloway, he had a band boy named Harold Holder, the same type as you were just mentioning -- a very sharp cat, very intelligent man; a good dresser, and very dignified. He was Cab Calloway's personal valet, and another kid who you know, and of course, I know, which we consider, or at least I consider, the epitome of all band boys and valets was Rudolph Rillis.
Rudolph Rillis, that is right -- he was THE band boy.
